name: Fenside Crofter
title: Crofter, drowned out
examine: Off the First Road crofts, the wet still on them. Under sacking by day and two families to a cottage by night, with the sheep on a common nobody gave them.
lines: The water came up in the night. We did not hear it. You do not hear water, that is the trouble with it.
The corn is cut. It is standing on boards at the crofts going green waiting for somebody with legs. Anybody at all.
The wall folk let the sheep stand on their stone. Ask them nothing. They will tell you a number.
Six ewes and the lamb. The stone folk counted them onto the wall and I counted them off it. Same number both ways.
His common is grass. Ours is ash. I will move them when there is somewhere to move them to.
The fire is small on purpose. Sit if you are sitting.
